sentence: This project builds deep learning models that estimate the pace of brain aging from MRI to help judge Alzheimer's disease risk.
This project studies how cell division works in apicomplexan parasites that cause malaria and other infections, in a search for drugs.
This project develops a gene editing treatment for Best disease, an inherited disease that causes progressive loss of central vision.
This project studies what circular RNA molecules do in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas.
This project uses imaging and genomic signatures to study how glioblastoma and meningioma brain tumors change over time.
This project uses cardiac modeling and simulation to help plan surgery.
This project tests whether cerebral perfusion imaging can find stroke patients with blocked vertebral or basilar arteries who benefit from thrombectomy.
This project studies how stigmatizing documentation about patients relates to how clinicians and patients talk and to patient experience of care.
This project builds technology that makes data and laboratory tools of molecular science usable by people with blindness.
This project studies how a bacterium used as an immunotherapy of cancer turns the immune system against bladder cancer.
This project develops a test that uses a panel of genes to spot kidney transplant patients whose rejection will resist treatment.
This project creates tools that use artificial intelligence to make clinical and low-field brain MRI scans work with research software.
This project studies how cells fuse the cell surface to internal membrane structures when their shape or size changes quickly.
This project uses mouse models to study how citrate levels affect brain excitability in a rare genetic epilepsy.
This project studies how too much aldosterone in the blood harms the function of small vessels in the brain.
This project brings together work on germ cells, the cells that pass genetic material to the next generation through egg and sperm.
This project studies how antibodies against the fusion peptide of HIV-1 suppress the virus.
This project studies how inputs onto cholinergic interneurons in the mouse nucleus accumbens shape the firing of those cells.
This project uses optical voltage imaging to find out how different types of cells contribute to field potential signals in the neocortex.
